REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 9, 2020 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 9, 2020, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor John Buell, Church in Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division Basketball League
  Pee Wee Division team - Raptors.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Academics Meets Athletics Cerritos Steelers Teams – Flag 6 and Under, Junior Clinic 8
  and Under, Clinic 10 and Under, Junior Pee Wee 11 and Under, and Pee Wee 13 and
  Under (2019 Orange County Jr. All American Super Bowl Champions).

  A brief update on the upcoming Tuesday, March 3, 2020 Cerritos General Municipal
  Election was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Viviana Gomez, representing Assemblymember Cristina Garcia, provided information
  regarding the Assemblymember’s “Woman of the Year” Program.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding traffic safety in the community, pesticides, the City
  budget, and the sales tax measure.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  December 12, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

7C.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of December 12, 2019:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1031, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration by Mayor
  Pro Tem Yokoyama.

  Councilmember Pulido recused himself from participation in this item and left the
  dais and the Council Chamber.

  A staff report was provided by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water
  and Power.

  Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama read into the record content from two documents
  described as emails transmitted by the Principals of Whitney High School and
  Wittman Elementary School to parents. The content expressed concerns regarding
  the addition of the Shoemaker Avenue truck route (The documents are public record
  and full-text copies can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).
 City of Cerritos  January 9, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  Mayor Pro Team Yokoyama also noted his opposition to the addition of the truck
  route on Shoemaker Avenue.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS: A motion was made by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to
  disregard Ordinance No. 1031, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE
  ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES, and direct staff to draft a new ordinance for
  City Council consideration with no truck route to be located between Shoemaker
  Avenue and 166th Street (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not carry (2 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Edwards, Solanki
  ABSENT:  Pulido (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION DID NOT PASS: A motion was made by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards,
  to waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1031, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not carry (2 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki
  NOES:  Hu, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  Pulido (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  There was no further action taken on this item.

  Austin Chu spoke in opposition to the use of Roundup for weed abatement.

  Michael Wauschek spoke in opposition to the use of Roundup for weed abatement.

  Lynda Johnson, Field Deputy for Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn,
